verdict.for_whom: This is a great fit for players who enjoy methodical travel planning and cooperative world-building, but those who crave immediate action or dislike long, unskippable cutscenes should steer clear.

claims.claim: Reviewers report startup crashes and stability issues, including access violation errors.

citations.review_text: 5 years later and it still crashes on startup
download this and it don't work , ive tried everything

The very beginning teased a great story, gameplay wise it was also OK, but the stability...
Let's just say that for me the game turned out unplayable with "Access violation" being the main antagonist. There are plenty of reports of this issue yet developers support just lists a wide variety of possible causes and possible solutions(most of which are system related) and no true troubleshooting guide. I certainly don't plan blindly trying everything from the list on a perfectly fine system where everything works, cause the developers have no clue what's wrong with their game. What's more many of the solutions on the official support site come from players.
Funny thing is the director's cut edition has similar reports, however one of the patches supposedly improved the stability(yet forums are still full of players having issues with the game). So they basically admitted it wasn't the system after all but poor coding, yet to give the director's cut a try you have to buy a paid upgrade

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the early game features lengthy cinematics and cutscenes with limited ability to skip or quit out of them easily.

citations.review_text: Kinda mid. too many cutscenes. doesnt allow you to quit cutscene without alt+f4 the game or skip cutscene

79 Minutes in and it is mostly cinematics. I've run down some cliffs, delivered some boxes, run about, delivered some more boxes.

Quite possibly the game play might increase later in the game if you have the patience to wait for it, but I found it too boring. Would have refunded had I not gone past the 48hr cut off. Shame because it looks great and I had high hopes for it but I want to play a game not watch a movie. Feels like it would have been better suited being made as a movie.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the opening hours lack clear direction, tutorials, or guides explaining what to do.

citations.review_text: played for a half hour or so,.  no idea what to do or where to go, or anything .  no guide, no tutorial.  no thanks

I was very hype to get this game as was really looking forward to experiencing what others report to be an amazing game. 

Having got the game free as part of an NVIDIA promotion I have found the game to be rather lack luster.

It tackles a few genres of sci-fi, shooter, adventure rpg with horror elements. frankly I feel let down that each one of the genres lacked any real in depth playability. 

I stuck with the game for over 100 hours on Playstation (not one to easily give up before I have given a fair play but I couldn't commit any more time than this to a game I did not enjoy). Played this for about an hour on Steam to realise I was again flogging a dead horse...

The graphics were, as expected, fairly detailed and the weather effects and travel is impressive at parts. I did glitch several times even on the first mission at one point getting stuck inside of a rock to the point of having to quit and restart the mission.

I know that people really loved the fact they were playing as TWD's Norman Reedus. Personally no customisable character to associate with and a general dislike for the character model probably is the basis for my dislike of the game. 

The storyline did not inspire much emotion, it felt very slow driven for the parts I experienced. The control itself on mouse and keyboard felt very clunky and uncomfortable. On controller it did feel a little better but did leave little to the enjoyment factor.
For being an open world game it felt very linear with little to inspire once you were used to the storyline. 

The tutorial initial stage was about 15 hours long for me due to diverging initially to enjoy the graphics (how I got stuck in a rock). the cut scenes initially impressive then took me out of playing a game and watching Norman moan about things I didn't really care about with no customised interactions left me fairly bored. 

The customisation and upgrade of items is initially satisfying but then you hit a realisation that as this is the only custo…

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players continuing past the opening describe gameplay focused on cargo delivery and terrain navigation, noting excellent PC optimization alongside complaints about awkward menu navigation, slow-paced tutorials, and immersion-breaking product placement.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the opening hours feature an extremely slow pace and excessive tutorials.

citations.review_text: A pity, this game is so promising. Beautiful graphics, an amazing digitized cast, and an intriguing and mysterious story all play tug-of-war with frustrating issues. The core game play of hauling and balancing packages through a nightmarish post-unknown-disaster world is amusing to begin with.  But before even getting through the tutorial missions (or is the whole game a tutorial?), the player is saddled with incomprehensible menu systems to wade through, mechanics for operating and using equipment that requires far to many key presses and mouse choices, and confusing instructions about what you are supposed to do and where you should avoid...this game basically feels like the work that your protagonist is experiencing in the game. If that was the goal...well, well done. In fairness, it may just be a poor translation from console to PC controls...but I feel like I would have lost my marbles even sooner trying to navigate it on console controls. Like so many modern graphically intense movie-like games, it would make a great movie, and I suggest you watch a youtube walkthrough if you want to know the whole story because ultimately the GAMEPLAY IS NOT FUN.
first 2~hours start off EXTREMELY slow. made me put off starting the game for ages. eventually i just plowed through it and the game really opens up into something wonderful.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the core gameplay loop as centering on delivering cargo while balancing loads and navigating rugged terrain.

citations.review_text:
A game to my knowledge that has the most intriguing opening 2 hour sequence of all time. I've made people who have no idea about game watch the opening cutscenes like as a movie night it's that intriguing. Safe to say that the story here is phenomenal. Granted the amount of story telling and reiteration of already told story is also it's major drawback.

To start I'll talk about the gameplay loop, grab packages and deliver to another location. It is basically mail man simulator. But it is no where near as boring as I swear everyone made it out to be when it came out. Maybe because I'm the type of person to grab literally everything no matter what I spent many hours just scavenging and grabbing everything and doing most side orders to try and level up each city. When doing these deliveries the environments and landscapes look stunning. It is quite a beautiful game to look at. This same beautiful environment at times is a little confusing to navigate, you can actually walk up or climb up some rocks, others you can't. This coupled with the already buggy vehicles creates some interesting traversal dynamics. Like walking will almost never fail you, but vehicles are twice as fast and can carry like 20x the loads. But sometimes the vehicles cannot handle basic mountains but the clunky climbing is still more efficient then just walking so you work through clunk constantly. But vehicle handling and terrain geometry is probably the gameplays only pitfall. BT combat and MULE combat is extremely basic yet engaging. As is trying to stealth through BT's in the snow sequence of the game.

The soundtrack fits the game perfectly, like there are some proper bangers in here. Cutscenes are voiced and acted great, but once again the sheer abundance of talking and cutscenes is the games short coming. Like the opening sequence is so interesting and "WTF", then the game begins and you are taught things. Then a cutscene rexplains what you learnt. This happens too much. The middle portion of…

This is a strange game, that takes some getting used to, but I am enjoying it. The mechanics are pretty novel, and almost remind me of something like Crazy Taxi. Get to your destination as quick as you can with the minimum damage to your cargo. Eventually you'll learn if you evenly distribute cargo you'll fall over less, and start to get the hang of it. Weigh the decision of going through infested territory vs a longer route.

Pros:
- Decent graphics
- One of the most accurate depictions of hiking with a heavy load I've ever seen
- Interesting story
- Novel mechanics
- Norman Reedus

Cons:
- The control scheme on PC is.. odd. You get used to it eventually but at first the menus were frustrating.
- Things like a guy named 'Die-Hard Man' break the immersion a bit. A Kojimaism?
- Speaking of immersion breaking, the initial tutorials are this guy pinging you every 30 seconds. About stuff you probably figured out if you're a gamer. There's no way to turn it off as far as I can tell. He shuts up after a while. But games like HZD do the intro tutorials a bit more immersively. 
- Some of the Points of Interest are  bit cut and pasty. I get why you'd make the same building in a post-apocalyptic world, but come on people.

I don't get this game, that's the shortened review.

Death Stranding is a game about you being a delivery person in some sort of post-apocalypse that seems supernatural in nature, from what I can tell. Its heavily story focused for the most part.

Gameplay wise its mostly just getting from one point to the next on a map, and its all about balancing your load while getting there, and making use of equipment periodically. Its certainly unusual, and its not bad, but I won't say it drew me into the game either.

Story wise...okay its only been 3 hours and I'm still totally lost. Not to say I can't have some respect for a narrative that places you as part of an ongoing story, but there are some things that do need a bit of explanation. Namely [b]what the heck happened to cause this weird supernatural(?) apocalypse anyway.[/b] The characters do come across as genuinely human, however I honestly didn't find them terribly interesting.

And atmosphere, well enviornment wise, soundtrack, etc its certainly got a rather unique feel to it, but the problem being it has somewhat of a lack of variety. All around you are just mountains, rocks, and streams with grass. No trees, no real differences from place to place so far. It gets boring pretty quick.

Long story short, this might make a good TV show, but not a good game. Its got some interesting ideas, but they fail to entertain and draw me in. And I know 3 hours doesn't tell you much, but honestly 3 hours should be more than enough time to get hooked on a game or not.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight product placement, such as consuming Monster Energy drinks and using personal facilities, as immersion-breaking elements.

citations.review_text: This game is beautiful. Amazing graphics. No doubt about that. Yet I played for 6 hours and did not understand what is going on-the development is just slow! Quests are a bit strange and pointless. I feel like I'm a delivery guy from DHL.  You can leave and read messages to/from other players and like them, which feels like I'm on Facebook. Why do I need to gather likes? People play games to get away from this "new normal". Second thing that breaks the magic is the product placement of MONSTER. There is a whole interaction where you drink a monster, get some "bonus" and then can go pee! Who needs that? Who needs to be able to go and take a shower or ♥♥♥♥ in a GAME. Such a shame because the feel of the world and landscapes is top notch. Maybe this game is targeted at younger audiences, who are used to this? I did not like it and probably will not finish it.

citations.review_text:
Truly unique

This game has been out for ages and has been in my steam library longer than most prior to a first time play. I'm now 17 hours in and I guess i am just starting to get it. I expected it to be a long burn but also wasn't sure exactly what to expect. I have been playing Kojima games since the original MG. I love his approach and this is truly something else.
To be honest it is way more entertaining than i was expecting. I am truly excited to boot this up every time. its weird and unlike anything else.
If you are a true gamer then you owe it to yourself to play through this as it is truly something new.
thank you Mr Kojima for pushing things way outside the box.
Also... one of the most highly optimised games i've played on PC. i have a pretty serious machine and this thing barely makes the fans move whilst still looking better than most modern AAA titles.

Unbelievable game. Took me a few attempts to get hooked but god was it worth it. Ended up completing it on PS5 but it runs incredibly well and looks stunning on PC. Unique gameplay loop and incredible world and themes.

One of the all time greats.
running on 1080 GPU and a 2015 CPU and this game (without changing settings) runs with steady 120 FPS. Great game for old pc's

I think the first 2h of the game are kinda bad and don't fully put out what makes the game great.
A gem, give a it a good try, you will be marked for life.

Just finished Death Stranding and I honestly didn’t expect it to hit this hard.

At first, it feels slow and almost strange but give it time and it completely pulls you in. The world is hauntingly beautiful, the atmosphere is unmatched, and the sense of isolation somehow turns into something really meaningful. Every delivery feels like it matters, and building connections (literally and figuratively) becomes incredibly satisfying.

The soundtrack deserves a special mention perfectly timed and emotional without being over the top. And the story? It’s weird, deep, and very Kojima… but if you stick with it, it pays off in a big way.

It’s not your typical action game, and it won’t be for everyone but if you’re open to something different, it’s a genuinely unforgettable experience.

Definitely one of those games that stays with you long after you finish it.
Its a good story but the pace is (for me) is too slow

It's good sorta, the gameplay is some of my favorite but its bogged down by a lot of unnecessary tutorials and wayyyyyyy too much talking. The story is good but also a slow burn. I see what Kojima was trying to do and I can't say it entirely pays off based on how long it takes to tie up some threads. But if your only focus is gameplay, I really liked it.

Let it be known that after the first 2 hours, I rage quit, uninstalled this game and went to bed pretty pissed off.
Two days later, time for me to process the all thing and read some reviews and other players ratings and opinions, I decided to give it another try. And then it's just been a truly wonderful 55 hours experience.
This game won't suit everybody, I can totally understand that. But don't give up too soon, because it really worth the effort.
Great game. Really one of a kind.
Interesting story. The game is boring and slow to begin with but picks up the further you progress. It is however a story game. You don't play it for the sake of the gameplay really

4 words. I. LOVE. THIS. GAME. Open worlds are my absolute favorite and Death Stranding does not disappoint. From how perfectly crafted the missions in this game are, even side ones mind you, to the story itself. Don't get me started on the story. It is AMAZING. I won't spoil of course...but the answer is closer than you think! However, if I was to get a little picky with this, I'd say the start of the game is really confusing for a new player. I had no clue what timefall was for a while! Just stick with it though. Eventually you'll fall in love with this game. :)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features asynchronous multiplayer mechanics allowing players to utilize structures, signs, and infrastructure built by others to assist with navigation and deliveries.

citations.review_text:
★★★★★★★★★★

top 2 game of all time for me, absolute stunning from top to bottom with some of the most fluid and addicting movement in gaming. Sights i didnt think was possible in gaming with one of the most fun enjoyable gameplay loops ever. Such an amazing story with fantastic characters and a long enough story to justify the purchase of the directors cut for 10nzd on sale. The story whilst confusing at first really really takes shape the more you play and the game despite being delivering packages for 50 hours its still such a fun game with me telling myself one more package over and over again.

The atmosphere is unparrelaled with the online connectivity of other peoples builds and signs (something similar to dark souls / elden ring) is such a welcome addition, with fun building that actually impacts gameplay and how the world and strategy of delivering and routes work entirely. with the ability to pour collected resources into roads and zipline systems all in the idea to make delivering and connecting america that much easier and more efficient. You can tell an enourmous amount of effort went into crafting this indepth from the rivers and grasslands to the cliffs and rockmounds. Kojima left no room for any more perfection with death stranding and its an essentially flawless title that ive poured nearly 60 hours into without having an inkling of a bad time.

The 100% is very very grindy however as the main story equates to about 50/63 achievements and leads you to believe the last 12ish are gonna be easy. WRONG, these achievements are mega time consuming and very grindy with a plethora of things to achieve and obtain. While the grind is immense the game makes up for it by being addictingly fun with gorgeous breathtaking views and graphics. Such an amazing game seriously check it out
interesting and beautiful world,  enjoyed the gameplay and the online social aspect of leaving trails behind for other players. very cool

It’s obvious that Death Stranding is a game that will strongly divide players.
You’ll either be among those who feel annoyed and bored by the gameplay, or among those who take a simple kind of pleasure from it. Judging by the fact that I recommend it, you’ve probably guessed it already: I’m part of the second group.
That said, I’ll play devil’s advocate (to some extent): yes, it’s slow and yes, it can feel a bit repetitive. As for the slow, methodical aspect, it’s clearly intentional, and I never found the game frustrating. It’s not even that laborious, really—proof of that is that I never died in the game (at least during my open-world deliveries), and I didn’t fail a single delivery.
Repetitive? Not that much, since you don’t spend the entire game in the same areas and you unlock tools that make your job easier. In fact, repetitive or not, I found the world so beautiful and immersive that I never got tired of going back and forth and exploring these stunning landscapes—it’s extremely relaxing to me.
On top of that, one thing that really kept me invested in the game was this strong sense of contribution. First with the NPCs, with whom you can improve your reputation and unlock new things, but above all with other players. I take immense pleasure in building structures and knowing that they helped other players. And it works both ways: I feel a real sense of gratitude when I come across something left behind by another player that ends up helping me. I’ve never enjoyed the feeling of cooperation in a game as much as I did here—even though it’s technically a single-player game where you never directly meet anyone else.
As for the story, I think it’s incredible. We all thought “WTF” when we saw the first trailers, and yet everything ends up being very understandable and fairly coherent. It’s incredibly original. I tip my hat to Kojima for daring to go off the beaten path and letting his creativity run free. I think many of us are happy to play as Norman Reedus, but ho…

    + epic intro and the beginning of the game
    + great views, beautiful world
    + shared map with others
    + I loved the soundtrack

Cons:
    - the story logic-wise was terrible, it was inconsistent and the rules governing this world just didn't make any sense. Some examples:
        - unger calling his child "BB", not via name?
        - why Sam never noticed that his stomach scar is the same as on the dolls?
        - a lot of using of science-sounding words and ancient "wisdom", but used just to sound smart without really any sense
        - timefall doesn't seem to match the living-dead theme, it just speeds up time passage?

keyboard controls are ass, but otherwise a good game. Had a much better time on my PS4, but the graphics alone made me buy it for pc

citations.review_text:
Death Stranding was my personal Game of the Year 2019. I've completed it to 100% on almost every platform (Steam, PS4, Xbox) it's has been released on. Only exception is PS5, since I don't own one.

I absolutely love this game and consider it one of the most unique gaming experiences ever made. The world, the incredible path optimization, the emotional story, and Kojima's signature weirdness come together to create something unlike anything else.

Calling Death Stranding a "walking simulator" or a "delivery simulator" completely misses what the game actually is. Deliveries are only the foundation. The real experience is about rebuilding a broken world, connecting people, overcoming harsh environments, and helping other players through one of the most original asynchronous multiplayer systems ever created. Seeing bridges, roads, ladders, and other structures built by strangers appear in your world (and knowing your own creations are helping someone else) is still a brilliant concept.

The game isn't perfect. Vehicles can behave strangely on rough terrain, and earning every achievement requires a significant amount of grinding. Still, none of that takes away from what makes Death Stranding so special.

It isn't a game for everyone, but if it clicks with you, it becomes an unforgettable experience.

Pros:

+ One of the most original games ever made
+ Fantastic story and memorable world
+ Brilliant asynchronous online system
+ Relaxing yet engaging gameplay loop
+ Outstanding soundtrack and atmosphere
+ Incredible sense of exploration

Cons:

- Vehicles can behave awkwardly
- 100% completion requires a lot of grinding
- Slow pacing isn't for everyone
- Some gameplay systems take time to appreciate

Maxed and 500L'd this game, loved the cinematics, loved the different play modes, I even enjoyed the third person shooter dynamic though yeah the combat became less about enjoying combat, and more about satisfyingly clearing out an area for "some time" by knocking the humans out, or snipping BTs.

I went all in on developing the road and zipline networks, ending up with mostly well-maintained L3 zips; the scarcity of chemicals and sometimes chiral crystals did make this an interesting non-core, non-side-quest, non-relevant, but immensely rewarding completionist part of the game. Why drive for 20 minutes when you can zipline for 10?

Meta-game-play tip: Once you complete the game, prop your phone nearby and max Legend deliveries (or LOL) to 500 (w/sound off) while watching Whitelight's 7 hour review.

You'll get to nod your head at the critiques of BT combat, but more importantly, relive the moments you loved/liked (personal: someone hugging "themself" -- so scifi-personal I love it).

And after that, watch some No More Bikes and wonder why Death Stranding is a Walking Game With No Sidewalks!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

My gripes:
BT combat yeah, but also, why not let me clear an area and then have the sun come out?
That slippery front-end of the van.
Chemicals shortage all the time for a L3 zipline network.
Ziplines don't auto-like so I never knew if anyone used my mountain peak zips -- crucial lack of likes there.
The L/LOL 500 orders compelled my completionist compulsion.
Yeah, yeah, some of the plot/logic holes, but they never derailed me.

Final note: Much of this game is about completing jobs and building things that others can use, and both of those things are just.... SATISFYING.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires watching lengthy credit sequences near the end.

citations.review_text: The game is good. But the ending is kind of BS, and the game actually forces you to watch the entire effing credits TWICE. First you must watch it, no matter what, because the game is not yet finished. The second time you can Alt+F4 out, of course, if you don't have unfinished business. If you do, according to Hideo Kojima, eff you and your time.

I rate this 3/5 stars.

The first star was lost due to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (sorry for language but it made me mad) credit scene. Not allowed to afk it, can't rubber band my controller due to button presses, lore dump that should've happened during the main game.

The second star was lost due to forcing me to go through it twice after a bsod.

With that out of the way, I genuinely enjoyed it. It's a casual package delivery game with spouts of horror and cheap jumpscares. The online sharing system could've been better and less other player dependant, but that's what you get for going with this style.

Edit: Oh nevermind, there's TWO credit scenes... The Dev team really are full of themselves aren't they? Another star removed. I do still recommend this game however.
